clue.text: Start to slate deficient Labour leader Miliband for proceeding at snail's pace?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, here taken from slate

parts.note: deficient means lacking or short, as in low on supplies
Michael Foot led the British Labour Party from 1980 to 1983
Ed Miliband, Labour leader at the time of the puzzle, supplies his first name

explanation.surface: A jibe at a sluggish Labour leader, slated for moving too slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: Two Labour leaders appear: 'Labour leader' is the past one, Michael Foot, and 'Miliband' gives the then-current one's first name, Ed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with slow feet moves sluggishly, the way a snail creeps along; the hyphenated adjective describes that.

clue.text: Cats finally sounding happy? That's encouraging

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word Cats

parts.note: a contented cat makes a low vibrating sound of pleasure, purring

explanation.surface: Contented cats make a noise that is taken as a good sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Urging someone on, as a rider does a horse with heels, is an act of encouragement; the participles match.

clue.text: A church led by males and as it appears to potential female bishops?

definitions.text: as it appears to potential female bishops

indicators.note: led by puts the males in front, ahead of what follows

parts.note: males are men
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A male-dominated church, as seen by women hoping to become bishops.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a wry view: to women seeking the mitre, a church run by men looks like a threat.
explanation.definitionFit: A threat or source of danger is how an obstructive male hierarchy would look to aspiring women clergy.

clue.text: Upper-class boy brought up in Scottish estate

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class usage

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the word for boy is written bottom to top

parts.note: a boy is a lad

explanation.surface: A posh lad raised on a Scottish landholding.
explanation.walkthrough: Udal tenure survives in Orkney and Shetland; 'brought up' suits a down clue, where the boy is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Udal is a form of freehold land tenure found in Orkney and Shetland, so an estate held that way.

clue.text: Relation in voluntary organisation turning up in European country

indicators.note: the second in places the reversed pair inside the name of the country

parts.note: Greece is a country in Europe

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the pair of words is written bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A family member working in a volunteer group shows up somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is fodder and the second is the container signal; 'turning up' flips the pair to ATNI.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's granddaughter is a family relation, one generation further down than a niece.

clue.text: One spending time at 23 across 24 — the end of the line

definitions.meaning: the queen who used the Isle of Wight house as her retreat and died there in 1901
a London railway terminus and Underground station of that name, where trains end their run

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is to the island retreat at 23 across; the second sense is the London terminus, the end of lines from the south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The monarch lived at Osborne on the Isle of Wight, and the station named after her is a major London terminus.

clue.text: See 11
Woman like Molly Malone without husband

indicators.note: without asks for the letter for husband to be dropped

parts.note: Molly Malone is the fishmonger of the Dublin song, so from Ireland

explanation.surface: A woman like the Dublin song's fishmonger, but unmarried.
explanation.walkthrough: Molly Malone is the heroine of the Dublin song 'Cockles and Mussels'.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris is a woman's first name, so it fits a clue asking for any woman.

clue.text: No natural listener, the boss — one getting spin introduced?

indicators.note: introduced means these letters are put into the word for the boss

parts.note: the boss is the leader
one is the Roman numeral I
PR is public relations, the business of spin

explanation.surface: A boss who doesn't listen well gets a spin doctor brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No natural listener' sounds like an insult to the boss, but describes a deaf person who reads lips; 'introduced' sends one and spin inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who follows speech by watching mouths is not hearing in the usual way, so is no natural listener.

clue.text: Intimate pub, "The Queen"

parts.note: an inn is a pub
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A cosy pub called The Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Intimate thoughts are private and closest to the heart, a synonym for innermost or inward.

clue.text: The Tories tell a whinger about 23 across's message

indicators.note: about means the letters are moved around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Conservatives telling a complainer the slogan of the Chancellor who shares a name with the royal house.
explanation.walkthrough: George Osborne, Conservative Chancellor, used the slogan from 2009 to argue that austerity was shared; 23 across shares his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The slogan was the Chancellor's signature claim of shared sacrifice, so it is aptly his message.

clue.text: After start of affair longs to get letters

indicators.note: after places the longing word behind the opening letter
start of picks the opening letter of affair

parts.note: to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: Once an affair starts, desires get letters written.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' looks like love letters, but means the names of the letter H.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the eighth letter of the alphabet is spelt out as a word; several of them are letters.

clue.text: Zero elasticity in arch

parts.note: zero looks like the letter O
a material with elasticity has give

explanation.surface: A rigid arch with no flexibility.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointed Gothic arch, or a diagonal rib in vaulting, is the architectural term here.

clue.text: Chemical separation could be produced by rinses? Yes

indicators.note: could be produced by suggests the letters of these words being reworked into something new

explanation.surface: A chemistry question: can rinsing produce a separation? Yes.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names the separating out of liquid from a gel, as whey from curd, a chemical process.

clue.text: Ability to absorb liquids comes from various openings in middle of tissue

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the central pair
middle of picks the central letters of tissue
various means the letters come in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Absorbency explained by the many pores in the middle of a tissue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges the openings as PONGINES, which sits 'in' the centre of tissue.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponge soaks up water, so the quality of being sponge-like is the capacity to soak up liquid.

clue.text: Soldiers who keep the machinery going?

definitions.meaning: read literally, the men who service machines, mechanics

explanation.definitionFit: Members of the forces are known collectively by this word, which also reads as engineers who maintain equipment.

clue.text: A trip with the legwork would be disastrous for me

definitions.text: A trip with the legwork would be disastrous for me

indicators.note: a disaster wrecks things, so these letters are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A high-wire performer explains that a stumble on the job would be fatal.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is spoken by the performer, for whom one slip of the feet means a fall; 'with' only joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-wire artiste walks a taut cable, so a trip while working would be disastrous for them.

clue.text: See 11
Birds with glossy appearance heading north — half of those off course will be trapped

indicators.note: will be trapped means the shortened word goes inside the reversed one
in a down clue, heading north means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: sleek fur or hair is smooth and glossy

indicators.note: half of keeps only the first three letters of the six

parts.note: strays are those that have wandered off course

explanation.surface: Sleek birds fly north, catching half the strays on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading north' turns the glossy word into KEELS; 'half of' keeps the first three letters of the strays, which 'will be trapped' inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Kestrels are small hovering falcons, a kind of bird of prey.

clue.text: Sort of politician expected to keep them open-mouthed?

indicators.note: to keep means the word for expected holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: something due is expected
'em is the clipped form of them
agog means eagerly amazed, open-mouthed

explanation.surface: A rabble-rouser is expected to leave his audience gaping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'them open-mouthed' is a phrase in the clue's colloquial voice; 'to keep' places it within expected.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabble-rouser who wins support by stirring popular passions is the kind of politician meant.

clue.text: Keep quiet about employment in the 6 and 21?

indicators.note: about means the word for keep quiet goes round the other piece

parts.note: to keep mum is to stay silent
employment of something is its use

explanation.surface: Stay silent about where you work in the Victoria and Albert.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 and 21 are VICTORIA and ALBERT; the definition is the word that follows them in the name of the London institution known as the V&A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victoria and Albert is a great London collection of art and design, so the place is a museum.

clue.text: Very short attack

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to assail is to attack

explanation.surface: A very brief attack.
explanation.walkthrough: A musical tempo marking, as in allegro assai, very fast.
explanation.definitionFit: In musical directions the Italian term means very, intensifying a tempo marking.

clue.text: Prince gives warning about bishop

indicators.note: about means the warning word goes round the letter for bishop

parts.note: an alert is a warning
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A prince warns of a bishop's plotting.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Albert was Queen Victoria's consort, here given the royal title.

clue.text: Satirist aiming dart at fashion

parts.note: to dart is to rush
ton is fashion or style, the bon ton

explanation.surface: A satirist takes aim at the fashion world.
explanation.walkthrough: Willie Rushton was an English satirist and cartoonist, co-founder of Private Eye; 'aiming' and 'at' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Willie Rushton made his name lampooning politicians, so he is a satirist.

clue.text: Industrial area is rougher with characters regularly getting bumped off

indicators.note: every other letter of rougher is removed, leaving the alternate ones

explanation.surface: An industrial area becomes rougher, with characters regularly murdered.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ruhr is Germany's industrial heartland.
explanation.definitionFit: The German valley of coal mines and steel works is the classic industrial region.

clue.text: Old bird turns over, somersaulting into great river, making a retreat on island

indicators.note: into places the flipped letters inside the river's name

parts.note: the Great Ouse is a river in eastern England

indicators.note: somersaulting means the run of pieces is flipped end to end

parts.note: a hen is a bird
to turn over a ... is to rob it

explanation.surface: An old bird somersaults into a river, which makes an escape to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somersaulting' flips the whole run to SBORNEHO, which goes 'into' the river after its first letter; 'turns over' is a burglar's turning over a house.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Victoria's Isle of Wight home was a royal retreat on an island off the south coast of England.

clue.text: Nothing works, sorry!

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
OPS is the plural of op, short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A clumsy apology when nothing is working.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of apology after a small blunder, like whoops.

clue.text: See 23
Excellent setter's brilliant clue getting misprinted

parts.note: brilliant means super, first-rate

indicators.note: a misprint swaps one letter for another, here the opening letter of clue

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler's fine clue is spoilt by a printing error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the crossword compiler but is a substance that sets; 'getting misprinted' changes the C of CLUE to G.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast-acting adhesive sets hard, so it is an outstanding setting agent.
